Confirmed and verified as the unique outlier. migrations/039_fix_art_job_unique_constraint.ts:12 imports the singleton `db` from ../src/db/db.js, its signature (line 14) takes NO db argument so it ignores the handle the runner passes via db.transaction(() => migrateFn(db)) (migrate.ts:209-213), and it never calls recordMigration. Confirmed mechanism. reopenTicket (tickets.ts:174-179) runs an unconditional `UPDATE ... SET status='open' WHERE id=?`. The partial unique index idx_modmail_open_unique ON modmail_ticket(guild_id,user_id,status) WHERE status='open' exists (db.ts:193-199). The reopen-by-userId path selects the most recent status='closed' ticket (threadReopen.ts:46-56) and is reachable via the `/modmail reopen user:` slash command (commands.ts:88). A closed+open ticket can coexist for the same user (the index only constrains status='open', so closing one and opening a new one is allowed), and flipping the old closed row to open then violates the index, throwing SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE caught at threadReopen.ts:150-153 as a generic 'Failed to reopen modmail thread. Check logs.' DM/unarchive side effects never run. However, integrity IS preserved by the constraint (the finding admits this) and the harm is only a confusing failure on an uncommon admin action, so the 'data-integrity'/medium framing overstates it. Downgraded to low.

Confirmed Discord API misuse. Refuted: the triggering precondition is unreachable. The finding assumes a row can be permanently_rejected=1 while its status is non-terminal (e.g. needs_info/submitted). I grepped every write of permanently_rejected in src: the ONLY path that sets it to 1 is rejectTx (reject.ts:87), and that same UPDATE sets status='rejected' (reject.ts:82). The vote-out path (actionRunners.ts:927-935) sets status='rejected' but never touches permanently_rejected. unblock (unblock.ts:189) only sets it to 0. Three in-code invariant comments confirm 'Permanently rejected apps have status=rejected with permanently_rejected=1' (drafts.ts:193, listopen.ts:46, ensure.ts). Therefore permanently_rejected=1 always implies status='rejected', and rejectTx's terminal guard `if (row.status === 'rejected') return {kind:'already'}` (reject.ts:59) short-circuits BEFORE the UPDATE at lines 79-91 ever runs. The flag can never be clobbered to 0 by a normal reject. Defect cannot occur.

Refuted on reachability. The orphaned claim at claimHandlers.ts:90-101 (returns after the cross-row perm-reject check without clearClaim/unclaimTx) requires the claimed app row to be non-terminal (so claimTx succeeds) while a SEPARATE row for the same (guild_id,user_id) has permanently_rejected=1. That coexistence is not producible by any code path: (1) the sole `INSERT INTO application` (drafts.ts:211, inside getOrCreateDraft) is gated by a perm-reject check that throws 'User is permanently rejected' before the INSERT (drafts.ts:155-162); (2) the sole writer of permanently_rejected=1 (rejectTx) also sets status='rejected' (terminal); (3) unblock clears the flag to 0 rather than creating coexistence. The same-row case is also blocked because claimTx rejects terminal statuses approved/rejected/kicked (reviewActions.ts:79-83). The finding itself concedes only 'direct flag-setting' (manual DB tampering) could create the precondition. The cross-row check is therefore unreachable defense-in-depth (documented as intended), and the orphaned-claim outcome cannot occur via code. Per unreachable-path policy: real=false.

Confirmed. analyze.ts:377 emits `Role can assign/remove ${role.position} roles below it.` but role.position is the Discord hierarchy position index, not the count of roles beneath this role. The loop only computes rolesAbove (line 369) and never computes a roles-below count, so the position integer is substituted as if it were that count. A staff role at position 50 with 3 roles beneath it would report it can assign/remove 50 roles. This is misinformation inside a 'ManageRoles Scope Warning' security advisory generated by /audit security and shown to leadership. Detection logic is fine; only the interpolated number is wrong. The proposed fix (filter roles with r.position < role.position excluding @everyone) is correct. Medium severity is reasonable for misleading security-advisory output.

Confirmed. threadReopen.ts:73 does `new Date(ticket.closed_at).getTime()` on closed_at, which closeTicket (tickets.ts:165) writes as datetime('now') into a TEXT column (db.ts:187), producing 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' with no 'Z'. V8/Node parses that space-separated form as LOCAL time; I empirically reproduced a 5h skew vs the UTC-normalized parse on a UTC-5 host. The 7-day boundary (line 77) is therefore shifted by the host UTC offset, taking the wrong branch (new thread vs reopen) near the boundary. The codebase's own normalizer (reviewCard.ts:108-111) does replace(' ','T')+'Z' and is omitted here; the sibling dashboardBridge.ts:304 repeats the bug. Boundary-only impact on non-UTC hosts keeps this at medium, not higher.

Confirmed mechanism. insertJoinStmt uses INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on (guild_id,user_id,channel_id,joined_at_s) with second resolution (line 25-26, 58); the UNIQUE constraint is exactly that 4-tuple (migration 052:27). Mechanism confirmed: securityAuditScheduler.ts:349 uses setInterval(async () => {...}) with no in-flight/reentrancy guard, and setInterval does not await the callback, so a run exceeding the interval overlaps the next. runSecurityAudit posts leadership-ping messages on critical/dangerous findings (lines 169-198) and generateAuditDocs saves a snapshot, so overlapping runs could duplicate pings/snapshots. Real latent defensive-coding gap (a reentrancy guard is the standard pattern and the proposed fix is correct), but downgraded from medium to low: overlap is rare under the 30-min cadence and the worst case is non-destructive duplicate pings, not data loss or a security breach.

Refuted empirically. The finding claims the 'end' listener registered at command.ts:444-446 (after awaiting exportPromise) can miss the event because csv.ts:253 calls stream.end() before streamReviewActionsCSV resolves, hanging the promise forever. streamReviewActionsCSV (csv.ts:144-272) is async but contains ZERO awaits (synchronous better-sqlite3 + stream.write, then end()), so its promise resolves on a microtask after the synchronous body. Confirmed: getAuditLog and getActionTypes (audit.ts) are fully synchronous better-sqlite3 calls (db().prepare(...).get/.all, no await; verified lines 55-75 and 90-166). The load wraps cached(...) in Promise.race against a setTimeout(8000) reject (audit/+page.server.ts:50-58). Synchronous SQL blocks the Node event loop for its full duration, so the setTimeout callback cannot fire until after the work completes, at which point cached() has already resolved and wins the race. The 8s timeout therefore cannot interrupt the query and the 504 branch is effectively dead. This is a correct, well-known event-loop-blocking architectural defect. Medium retained: the queries are reasonably bounded (keyset pagination, FTS index, LIMIT 200 name lookup, default 7-day window), so a true multi-second freeze is possible but not the common case.
